human_tolerance.notes: Wikipedia: occupies the outskirts of human dwellings such as compounds and gardens, is commonly found near garbage bins, tunnels through brick and masonry, and is a serious pest in poultry farms.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: No breeding calendar is given in the cited sources (Wikipedia reports 8-10 litters per female in her lifetime, with no months). The phase spans the year as a placeholder, not as a measured season.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon 45664 via Wikidata P3151 and checked against the iNaturalist taxa API on 2026-10-31 (rank species, active). ITIS TSN 585161 via Wikidata P815 and checked against the ITIS full record. GBIF 2437729 is the accepted species key.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); Wikidata P627 = IUCN ID 2541. Wikipedia infobox also reports LC (IUCN 3.1).

range.note: Country codes converted from Wikipedia's list: Bangladesh, China, India, eastern Pakistan, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam. Taiwan is deliberately excluded from native: the status there is contested. Most literature treats the population as probably introduced, while fossil evidence suggests Pleistocene presence. The record therefore does not assert native status in TW. Presence in TW is supported by occurrence records, not by range status.

traits.body_plan.note: Mammal rodent of the family Muridae (Wikipedia, Greater bandicoot rat).

traits.limb_count.note: Wikipedia describes dark feet with light-coloured claws; four limbs follow from the mammalian body plan.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Only walking is declared. Wikipedia describes feet with claws and burrowing, but gives no gait or speed data. Climbing and swimming are not declared; no source was found for them.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Mammal; endothermy follows from the class.

traits.skin.note: Wikipedia: dark grey-brown fur with long black hairs; scaly, naked tail.

traits.nest_type.note: Wikipedia: 'characteristic large burrows give away their presence' and the species 'can tunnel through brick and masonry'.

traits.perching.note: No perching is described in the source; set false for a ground-dwelling rat.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg (0.72 kg, Small < 1 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 719.96 g (species-level, Ref_117 Smith et al. 2003), converted to kg. Wikipedia gives no mass. A popular-web value of 0.5-1 kg was seen in search results but is not an openly licensed citation, so it was not used.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia: head-and-body length about 30-45 cm (midpoint 0.375 m); tail up to 28 cm, which is a maximum rather than a typical value. 0.375 + 0.28 = 0.655 m, rounded to 0.65 m. This is an upper-leaning estimate of nose-to-tail length, not a measured mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia (Reproduction): 'The lifespan of adults is around a year.' The statement is not qualified as wild or captive, and it is used here as the typical adult lifespan. No captive or wild maximum is used. Low confidence.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits gives Diet-Inv 20% and Diet-PlantO 80% (Ref_1 Nowak 1999, certainty ABC). The split of the 80% plant share into seed 0.4 and graze 0.4 is authored from Wikipedia's mention of 'household refuse, grain, and vegetables'. The 0.4/0.4 split is judgement, not a measurement. Household refuse is handled as the 'compost' resource, not as a diet entry.

traits.social.note: Judgement from Wikipedia: 'If caged with other bandicoots, it is likely to fight to death within a few hours.' Solitary is an authored value.

traits.defense.note: Judgement. Wikipedia describes erect guard hairs, grunts and aggression when disturbed. The Flee defense is the closest allowed value for a rodent that tends to retreat to burrows; it is not a source statement.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, not a measurement. Wikipedia says the species 'occupy the outskirts of human dwellings' and is 'commonly found near garbage bins', which suggests tolerance of people.

habitat.note: Ground use from EltonTraits ForStrat G (certainty A). Fossorial share 0.2 is an authored estimate from Wikipedia's description of large burrows and tunnelling, and is not a time-budget measurement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Quoted from Wikipedia's description of near-dwelling behaviour; urban_affinity Adapter is judgement.

seasonal.note: No seasonal calendar is supported by the sources. Strategy ActiveYearRound is the authored default for a rodent with no dormancy source. The breeding phase spans the year as a placeholder; the juvenile duration 55 days is the midpoint of Wikipedia's 'sexual maturity around 50 to 60 days after birth'.

behavior.note: fsm-ground-forager-v1 is a ground-dwelling mammal program with flee, forage, rest and drink states. Nocturnal default rest window used. food_tag set to seed (grain). Program fit is judgement from Wikipedia's account of a ground-foraging, burrow-using pest.

look.note: Authored colour and proportion values. Palette: dark grey-brown upper parts with light ventral fur and a dark tail, from Wikipedia's description. Proportions are judgement.
